title: Correct a transcribed Figure 3 dose-label mismatch in the wulfenite record
body:
Independent review of Cai et al. (2024), DOI 10.3390/molecules29225404, original page 5 Figure 3, confirms that both the intermediate optical panel and the corresponding Raman trace are labelled Na2S/PbMoO4 = 0.05. The new record instead says the labels differ (0.5 versus 0.05), and its source dossier repeats that unsupported contradiction.

The initial immutable observation is `reviews/structured/20261015T051448Z-wulfenite-round88-dose-label-initial/review.yaml`, F1, stable issue key `wulfenite-round88-figure3-dose-label-transcription`. It binds the complete publisher PDF and a high-resolution rendering. This is a minor record transcription defect; the chemical leaching results and other source limitations remain supported.

Acceptance:
- Remove the claimed 0.5/0.05 mismatch from mechanism context, second evidence explanation, and corresponding source-dossier entries.
- Preserve the actual PbS solubility contradiction, time-series uncertainty, assay denominators and laboratory scope.
- Append canonical EDIT/inline history, preserving CREATE and the initial review.
- Revalidate the affected record and completed batch; save an independent successor explicitly resolving the exact F1 occurrence.

title: Clarify chromium partitioning and assay definitions in the IPS21 leather-shavings study
body:
The new chromium-tanned-leather-shavings record uses Wieczorek et al. (2023), DOI [10.1128/spectrum.02749-23](https://doi.org/10.1128/spectrum.02749-23), as qualified evidence of laboratory matrix bioconversion and chromium partitioning. It does not assert an isolated chromium product, a recovery percentage or industrial deployment.

The complete original JATS/HTML, Tables 1–2, Figures 1–5 and all five supplemental PDFs were inspected. Several source uncertainties prevent stronger claims:

- Figure 4 stacks liquid and solid-residue total-Cr concentrations labelled g/kg. The digestion procedure does not define a common normalization basis or provide fraction masses and a closed chromium inventory. The Results assign 10.31 g/kg to the 0.1% yeast supernatant, whereas the plotted value near 10 is in the 1% uninoculated supernatant.
- Table 1 reports larger source-labelled degradation rates at 1% than 4% shavings, contrary to the text's optimum narrative. The rate is described as calculated from biomass concentration, without an explicit equation separating residual shavings from yeast biomass.
- The abstract's 5 g/L NaCl and stock-medium method's 2.5 g/L do not establish one unambiguous final liquid recipe. The inoculum OD600 is printed as `1,000`.
- Supplemental file 3b identifies laboratory sample C/1306 as Yarrowia lipolytica but lacks an explicit IPS21 crosswalk; its October 2021 report and February 2022 sequence printouts are not reconciled with the main text's sequencing date.

Acceptance requires a legitimate original correction, author-supplied public clarification or independently reproducible source data that resolves the relevant normalization, arm labels, degradation equation, recipe and strain mapping. Preserve the current primary and SI byte hashes, document any new version, and independently review any materially expanded record. Cr(VI) nondetections in SI2 remain censored at the stated ≤1 mg/L liquid and ≤1 mg/kg residue bounds; combined biomass/feed residues do not prove intracellular exclusion.

This is a source-evidence follow-up, not a currently demonstrated defect in the qualified record. It should remain open while these source limitations are unresolved.

title: Clarify the gypsum dehydration control annotation, later inoculum loading, and missing supplementary evidence
body:
The bounded round88 curation preserves two mineral identities and a disputed biological interpretation. It does not establish microbial water extraction or mineral recovery. The gypsum and anhydrite records share the same original experiment, correction, correspondence and independent counterexperiment.

Evidence requiring clarification:

- Huang et al. 2020, DOI 10.1073/pnas.2001613117, original Figure 3E: the caption defines black squares as anhydrite, and a square appears inside the No microbe panel despite main prose reporting anhydrite absence. Its position does not establish a resolved control peak. Please obtain attributable clarification of that annotation and the exact control diffractogram, including the lighting arm, initial phase check and phase detection limit. Do not infer a control mineral fraction from the marker.
- Douchi et al. 2024, DOI 10.1093/pcp/pcad139: the 15-day polycrystalline-chip Results report 3 micrograms chlorophyll/chip, whereas Methods report 200 micrograms/mL with 100 microliters deposited, equivalent to 20 micrograms/chip. Obtain attributable arm-specific loading/protocol clarification. The Methods Cu K-alpha presentation and Figure 1B Co label also require consistent diffraction-axis metadata if numerical peaks are later reused.
- Obtain genuine original supplementary files for both publications by a new legitimate route. The inspected routes yielded 403 responses, error XML or challenge HTML, all excluded. In particular, Douchi Supplementary Figure S1 is required before adopting the 30-day oriented-crystal/scraped-surface diffraction outcome as independently inspected evidence; Huang supplemental facet/humidity/microscopy claims remain outside the accepted scope.

The formal Huang correction DOI 10.1073/pnas.2021524117 already resolves coupon dimensions to 5 × 8 × 0.5 mm. That issue is not open. The 2020 reply DOI 10.1073/pnas.2018184117 is a clarification of the original study, not an independent replication. The fully inspected main Douchi Figure 1 supplies a qualified independent 15-day negative result despite remaining protocol differences.

Acceptance requires preserved source bytes and acquisition provenance, inspection of relevant original graphics/controls, and a narrowly scoped record update with canonical EDIT history and independent successor review if accepted claims change. Do not close this issue merely because both records pass schema validation. Keep it open if no attributable clarification is obtained; no author contact is authorized by this issue draft.

Local evidence inventory: research/sources/round88-minerals/20261015T051426Z-source-investigation.json. Raw source hashes: Huang main HTML f196912cfe9952ca400d30b6c052950d33cafe590a19d6d20dd378cb0ba5a135; Figure 3 SHA 8866032eec2457ee2112a0b7fec05eabca4f1c92d2e4e2f8f53845fd8518fc44; Douchi main HTML b6abc740458a25e0544f7924593059eaeb1f1ad4f9cf7e20b56931e66e97d928. The complete inventory supplies every original figure path, URL and SHA256. Bounded all-state issue search found no exact-study DOI/strain match; it does not claim exhaustive absence of related calcium-sulfate topics.

title: Correct the stale round and cohort heading in the round88 ingest-report builder
body:
Independent package review found that the new round88 manifest builder retained the previous round's Markdown heading, `Round87: three reviewed material records`, although this batch contains five records. The builder has not yet published the report, and no scientific owner is affected.

The immutable local initial observation is `cmm-round88-builder-static-initial-20261015T052255Z.json`, OP1, stable key `round88-manifest-heading-stale-cohort`. Its evidence and exact builder snapshot will be retained with the PR's publication evidence.

Acceptance: correct only the stale heading to `Round88: five reviewed material records`; independently compare the changed builder against its captured predecessor; verify both generated report formats identify the same current five-owner cohort; retain an explicit successor disposition. This is an operational reporting correction, not a new scientific claim.
